answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because ivory only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, river is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any nebula approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
